An area of approximately 40 acres has been designated as a spoil area and construction yard. This area is bounded by the 1,960-foot contour and a graded slope at one end and has a storage capacity of approximately 4 million cubic yards of spoil materials. The area would be built as spoil material becomes available, with drainage provided to handle runoff. Upon completion of the project, the 40-acre spoil area and construction yard would be forested, with the exception of an area to be used for a future 525-kV switch-yard. The switchyard area would be stabilized, planted, and maintained with grass or other cover until needed for switch-yard use.
The Applicant would rely on Federal Power Commission Order No. 414, "Guidelines for the Protection of Natural, Historic, Scenic, and Recreational Values in the Design and Location of Rights-of-Way and Transmission Facilities," in the design and construction of all transmission facilities. The esthetic impact of the transmission line would be minimal and would not interfere with any recreational activities. New right-of-way areas would be blended with the surrounding areas so that the contrast between cleared areas and natural areas would be minimized. Selective cutting would be utilized where feasible, and low-growing vegetation would be left at road crossings to screen the view of the transmission in-Road crossings that are bare of vegetation would be plante. with low-growing plants where practical to provide a screen. No herbicides would be used in clearing or maintaining the rights-of-way.
Plans for restoration and enhancement of project lands during operation and maintenance are presented in the Exhibit W, pages 3-4 thru 3-6 as amended. The Applicant would provide adequate natural screening to minimize the view of the reservoir from the nearby highways and overlooks.
4.2.2 Water Quality and Aquatic Biota
Applicant is considering the necessity and desirability of augmenting stream flows in Howard Creek with water from the Bad Creek Reservoir. The flow augmentation system could be used continuously or intermittently to add flow to Howard Creek. Natural seepage could also partially compensate for reduced flows caused by operation of the project.
